description: Graphiti, self-hosted with telemetry off, building its temporal knowledge graph in Neo4j from one arm's dated revision stream (PREREGISTRATION.md sections 8, 11 and 13). adapter.py and ingest.py implement this configuration; README.md describes it.

graphiti_core.dependency_versions: every package at the version that graphiti-core's own uv.lock pins at the release (in graphiti_core-0.31.2.tar.gz, SHA-256 cee47010d440ae015646c722b18272c3b2e659e38ab7ed6a0fd165a15282f451)

graph_database.auth: none (NEO4J_AUTH=none); Neo4j is on the internal network only
graph_database.restart: unless-stopped: a Neo4j that stops is restarted, and the ingestion run it interrupted stops with exit status 2, to be resumed
graph_database.store: one named volume per run (the compose project's neo4j-data), so that each arm has its own store and arms never share one

llm.sampling: no request carries temperature, top_p or top_k: the client's temperature is the SDK's omit sentinel (anthropic.omit), which the SDK leaves out of the request
llm.max_tokens_source: Graphiti's own resolution: LLMConfig's default, DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS, unless a Graphiti call site gives its own
llm.request: Graphiti's own code path: its prompts and its forced tool call (tool_choice naming its response model's tool); it sends no thinking or output_config field
llm.anthropic_client: asofbench_systems.llm.make_async_client: anthropic.AsyncAnthropic with base_url https://api.anthropic.com given in code (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is never read), the key read from the Docker secret /run/secrets/anthropic_api_key only, the SDK's own httpx client honouring HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY, max_retries 8, timeout 600 s
llm.usage_log: asofbench_systems.usage.instrument wraps client.messages.create and records every response in usage.jsonl under the episode being ingested

embedder.use: voyage-4-nano-document (the model's document prompt) for every text Graphiti embeds while ingesting, the stored texts and the name searches it makes to deduplicate them; the answering path builds a second embedder with voyage-4-nano-query (the query prompt) for questions
embedder.dimensions_parameter: not sent: OpenAIEmbedder asks for the model's own 2048 dimensions and keeps the first embedding_dim (2048) of them
embedder.server: env/embedder (asofbench/embedder): voyage-4-nano on the CPU in float32 behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint

prompts.query: Represent the query for retrieving supporting documents:

cross_encoder.raises: no reranking model is registered for asof-bench
cross_encoder.why: no system reranks with a model (section 11): Graphiti is given a cross-encoder whose rank raises, and searches only with reciprocal-rank-fusion recipes, so its default OpenAIRerankerClient is never created and nothing ranks with a model

search.while_ingesting: Graphiti's own duplicate searches: EDGE_HYBRID_SEARCH_RRF for edges (BM25 and cosine similarity fused by reciprocal rank) and exact names and a direct cosine-similarity search for nodes (_semantic_candidate_search), none with a reranker
search.answering: the answering path, added before any scored run: Graphiti.search with no center node, EDGE_HYBRID_SEARCH_RRF

episodes.group_id: the episode's corpus, pep or eth
episodes.order: within a group, one at a time in stream order, each awaited before the next; the two groups concurrently
episodes.saga: one saga per proposal, named by the episode's proposal id, with saga_previous_episode_uuid from the adapter's state (the proposal's last ingested episode)

previous_episodes.rule: previous_episode_uuids is the uuids of the same proposal's last 3 ingested episodes (Graphiti's EPISODE_WINDOW_LEN), all recorded before the episode, oldest first, and empty for its first episode; the saga predecessor is the last of them. Graphiti's get_by_uuids does not order the episodes it returns, so the window's order inside Graphiti's prompt is Graphiti's own

episodes.name: episode_id
episodes.episode_body: asofbench_systems.stream.render_episode, the one episode template of every store system

failures.order: within a group, episodes are ingested strictly in stream order, so that no episode is ingested after a later one of its group
failures.retries: Graphiti's own retries and the SDK's apply first; an episode that still raises is attempted twice more in place, after 30 s and then 120 s, with the same previous episodes and saga predecessor, and one that still raises is logged with ok false and never attempted again, by the run or a resumed one
failures.infrastructure: an infrastructure error stops the run with exit status 2 and leaves the episode unlogged, so that a resumed run attempts it again: Neo4j unavailable or a session lost (ServiceUnavailable, SessionExpired, SessionError, DatabaseUnavailable); the embedder unreachable or failing (openai APIConnectionError, InternalServerError); after the SDK's own retries, the API unreachable, rate-limited, overloaded or failing, or refusing the key (anthropic APIConnectionError, RateLimitError, OverloadedError, InternalServerError, AuthenticationError, PermissionDeniedError, and Graphiti's RateLimitError); so does a failed attempt that left the episode in the store
failures.consecutive_failures: 5 logged failures in a row in a group stop the run with exit status 3
failures.resume: ingest --resume continues each group from its first episode with no log line, on the stream and arm the run began with
failures.skip: ingest --resume --skip-episode <episode_id> logs the first episode of its group with no log line as failed (skipped by the operator after repeated infrastructure stops), records it in run.json and goes on
failures.lock: every invocation, the removal of episodes included, holds the output directory's lock: it creates run.lock with O_EXCL (flock and lockf do not exclude across containers on Docker Desktop's bind mounts), touches it every 30 s and removes it at its end; a second one stops at once with exit status 2; a SIGTERM cancels the invocation, which records itself and releases the lock; one killed outright leaves the lock, for the operator to remove once it is gone
failures.crash: an exception that no rule expects ends the invocation with exit status 4, which run.json records with the exception's class
failures.calls_that_raise: every call that raises after the SDK's retries is a usage line with no tokens and its exception's class, counted as api_errors, so that a failure Graphiti catches and carries on from stays visible

concurrency.source: Graphiti's DEFAULT_SEMAPHORE_LIMIT; SEMAPHORE_LIMIT is not set

telemetry: off: GRAPHITI_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false in the image and in the container, so Graphiti sends no telemetry event; Neo4j's usage report is off (dbms.usage_report.enabled=false); no route leads out but the one to the API

routes_out.through: the egress proxy (env/egress, asofbench/egress) on the internal network, which opens a CONNECT tunnel to that host and port only and refuses everything else
routes_out.for: the construction model, claude-haiku-5-5, which builds Graphiti's store

services_inside.name: neo4j
services_inside.holds: Neo4j 5.26 community and the graph Graphiti writes there, on the run's own volume

services_inside.name: embedder
services_inside.holds: the voyage-4-nano server and the model's weights

services_inside.name: egress
services_inside.holds: the egress proxy, the only container also on the network with a route out

network_policy.container: the graphiti container is on the internal network only (internal, with no address of the host on it) and sees its adapter and configuration, the run's input stream (read-only at /input), its output directory (/output) and the API key as a Docker secret
network_policy.unreachable: data/v0.1, every file of this repository other than the adapter and its configuration, the streams other than the run's input file, the corpus clones, and the corpora's live sources (github.com/python/peps, github.com/ethereum/EIPs, github.com/ethereum/ERCs, peps.python.org, eips.ethereum.org and ercs.ethereum.org), their mirrors or a clone of them
network_policy.provider_side_tools: none: no request carries a server tool (web search, web fetch, code execution, file search or any other); the one tool in a request is Graphiti's own client tool, the schema of its response
network_policy.checked_by: env/netcheck.py, run by ingest before anything is ingested, which aborts the run on any failure; its report is netcheck.json in the run's output directory

installed.lock: requirements.txt, compiled from requirements.in with hashes; the image installs it hash-checked, from wheels only

images.asofbench/graphiti: built from graphiti/Dockerfile with systems/ as the context, on the base image above
images.asofbench/egress: built from env/egress, on the base image above
images.asofbench/embedder: built from env/embedder, on the base image above, with env/embedder/requirements.txt and the model above
images.per_run: each run records the IDs of the four images it ran with, which its launcher gives in ASOFBENCH_IMAGE_IDS, in its run.json and summary.json
